records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — The unbounded guest array is materialized as bulk inserts, a full attendee reload, calendar update, and concurrent email fanout in one request, allowing a large request to exhaust database and mail capacity.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in organizer-add-guests-email.ts line 25, the replyTo header includes all attendees: `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`. This spreads all attendee emails into the reply-to header. As guests are added over time, this array grows unbounded. Email providers have header size limits (typically 8KB for headers), and exceeding these limits could cause email delivery failures. The diff shows this is new code being added, and there's no cap on the number of attendees that can be included in this header.

records.issue_text: apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42 — No dialog test covers mutation errors, so the always-truthy interpolated message can expose an undefined code instead of the intended fallback error.
records.rationale: The finding points to line 42 in AddGuestsDialog.tsx where the error message is constructed: `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\``. This interpolation will produce strings like 'undefined: translated_message' when err.data?.code is undefined, or 'CODE: undefined' if t(err.message) returns undefined. The fallback `message || t('unable_to_add_guests')` only triggers if the entire string is falsy, but template literals with 'undefined' are truthy strings. This is a real bug in error handling that could expose confusing error messages to users.
